To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the pathogenesis of renal disease in diabetes is complex and incompletely understood; 2. the currently used drugs are not very efficacious and have significant off-target side effects; 3. there is a need for new drugs that target the pathophysiology of renal disease and are safe; 4. the current clinical trials are not very successful; 5. the current clinical trial design is not appropriate; 6. the clinical trials should be redesigned to be more effective and
there are no new agents for the management of diabetic kidney disease.
there are no new agents that come close to solving the problem of diabetic kidney disease.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new drugs that can prevent or slow the development of diabetic nephropathy and the need to find new ways of using existing drugs to improve the outcomes of patients with diabetes.
the development of novel therapies to treat kidney disease in patients at risk for or with diabetes.
understanding the mechanisms of renal injury in diabetes and developing new therapeutic strategies to prevent or reverse the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no effective therapies for the treatment of diabetic kidney disease.
the current state of affairs in diabetic kidney disease is unsatisfactory and requires a new approach.
the search continues for a new and effective drug to treat diabetic kidney disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are still far away from the ideal treatment for diabetic kidney disease.
the current state of affairs in the treatment of kidney disease in patients suffering from diabetes is unsatisfactory and that new strategies are urgently required.
the current treatment options for diabetic kidney disease remain limited and that new approaches to managing this disease are urgently needed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a pressing need for the development and testing of new approaches to the treatment of kidney disease in diabetes.
the development of novel therapies for diabetic kidney disease remains an important unmet medical need.
we need to focus our attention on drugs that can slow or halt the progression of kidney disease, and that can do so in a safe and effective manner.
